memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Danielle chose the American nonstop pair for this Atlanta trip because its earlier Wednesday arrival and substantially larger Friday airport margin outweighed the small savings from a restrictive Delta Basic itinerary. This is an ordinary trip-specific choice and does not establish a recurring preference.

messages.content: I reconsidered Atlanta. I am going Wednesday evening and coming home Friday after the summit. Drop the East Point visit. Please recheck the nonstop flights, including the real cost and whether Friday leaves enough time to get my suitcase from the hotel.

For Wednesday, September 17, the two useful DFW-ATL nonstops are American at 4:35 p.m., arriving 7:42 p.m., and Delta at 6:10 p.m., arriving 9:18 p.m. Both protect Thursday's 2:00 p.m. sponsor workshop; the earlier flight simply gives you a more normal dinner and hotel check-in. What time does Friday's summit formally end, and will you check a bag?
It ends at noon. I will check one bag. The Residence Inn can hold it after checkout, but I do not want to leave the closing session early.

That makes the 3:35 p.m. Delta return possible but tight. Allow about 15 minutes to leave the summit, 15 to retrieve the bag, and 25-40 minutes to ATL. You would likely reach the terminal around 1:10-1:25, roughly 70-85 minutes before departure. The 5:55 p.m. American return gives you more than three hours at the airport even with traffic.
Compare the complete totals and ticket restrictions. I need to know whether the cheap fares are actually cheaper once the suitcase is included.

I found three sensible pairs. Delta Basic, 6:10 p.m. Wednesday and 3:35 p.m. Friday, is $356 airfare plus $70 for the checked bag, totaling $426. It is nonrefundable, has no voluntary changes, and the seat is assigned later unless purchased. Delta Main on the same flights is $436 plus $70, totaling $506; it is nonrefundable but can be changed with any fare difference. American Main Cabin, 4:35 p.m. Wednesday and 5:55 p.m. Friday, is $428 plus $80 for the bag, totaling $508. It is nonrefundable, but changes are allowed with a fare difference and standard seat selection is included.
So Delta Basic saves only $82 against American, but it gets me in later and makes Friday much tighter.

Correct. The $82 savings buys away most of your Friday margin and gives you a more restrictive ticket. Delta Main is only $2 less than American after baggage, so its later Wednesday arrival and earlier Friday departure provide no meaningful cost advantage.
Is there any concern that the 5:55 American flight is too late for the summit schedule, or that I am paying for another hotel night?

No. You would check out Friday morning, leave the suitcase with the hotel, attend the full summit, collect it after noon, and head to ATL around 1:00-1:15 p.m. The flight does not require a Friday hotel night. The Wednesday arrival does require two nights at the Residence Inn: Wednesday and Thursday.
And the American fare is still $508 all-in for the flight and one checked bag, with no seat fee unless I choose an upgraded location?

Yes. The ticket charges now are $428 round trip. The first checked bag is expected to cost $40 each way, paid separately, bringing the flight total to $508. Regular selectable seats are included; preferred or extra-legroom seats cost more. The bag fees can change before travel, so the $80 is not charged in today's ticket purchase.
Book American: 4:35 Wednesday to Atlanta and 5:55 Friday back to DFW. Use a regular aisle seat on both flights if one is open.

The American flights are ticketed for September 17-19 under confirmation H6R2QK. Outbound departs DFW at 4:35 p.m. and arrives ATL at 7:42 p.m.; return departs ATL at 5:55 p.m. and arrives DFW at 7:18 p.m. Regular aisle seats 18C outbound and 20D return are assigned. The card charge is $428. The expected $80 round-trip bag cost remains payable at check-in, so the working flight total is $508. The Atlanta plan is now Wednesday through Friday with two hotel nights; the Residence Inn still needs to be rechecked and reserved, and ground transportation remains an estimate.
